raw_response:
I am getting older, and there are only two of us in the house, so this year I still do what is steady and what my hands can manage. Wheat and maize on the same land is the safest for me because every year we do it this way and I know the timing. Cotton I keep on a smaller piece because it brings cash, but it needs more watching and picking, and at my age I cannot spread myself too thin. I do not read those technical papers, I just look at the field, remember last year, and do close to what worked. If I put too little fertilizer and the crop turns weak, that loss is bigger than saving a little money, but I also cannot spend all my cash at once. So I use moderate amounts, split the fertilizer when I can, and irrigate when the crop really needs it because pumping water costs money.
